Catholic Priests Killed in China.

Sir,

With reference to the attached cutting from the
"Shanghai Times" under date December 18, 1929, I have
to report that this statement is true as the particulars
given hereunder will show but this list includes missionaries
who met their deaths as far back as 1923 which makes a
total of 22.

| Name | Nationality | Mission | Date & Place where killed |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 Father Angello Melotto | Italian | Franciscan | Sept. 1923 at Tsianfu, E. Hupeh, killed by bandits. |
| 2 Father Achille Soenen | Belgian | Belgian Missions of Scheut-Brussels | Dec. 1923 at Satsji (Palskai) W. Mongolia, killed by revolting soldiers. |
| 3 Father Pitton | French | Paris Foreign Missions | 4/2/24 at Yunnan, killed by bandits. |
| 4 Father Aurelius Meirney | Spanish | Franciscan | 4/8/26 at Sianfu, Shensi. |
| 5 Father Ryufollart | Belgian | Belgian Missions of Scheut-Brussels | Sui Yuen, Longolia. |
| 6 Father Fred Lawens | Belgian | -- do -- | 20/8/26 at Si-wan-tse Mongolia. |
| 7 Father Duout | French | Jesuit | 24/3/27 at Nanking killed by soldiers |
| 8 Father Vanara | Italian | Jesuit | 24/3/27 at Nanking, killed by soldiers. |
| 9 Father Joseph Hou | Chinese | Secular | 30/4/27 at Tien, Kiangsi. |
| 10 Father Van de Bosch | Belgian | Belgian Missions of Scheut-Brussels | 20/9/27 at Shansi killed by bandits. |
| 11 ? | Chinese | (Killed along with Father Van de Bosch.) | |
| 12 Father H. Waeldele | German | Franciscan | 3/11/27 at Shansi by disbanded soldiers. |

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 18, 1929.
C. I. D. REGISTER
No. I. O. D. 861.
Date..8....1....30.

22 PRIESTS SLAIN
IN CHINA
San Francisco, Dec. 16.
The Rev. James Keller,
superior of the Maryknoll
Junior Seminary at Los
Altos, told an Associated
Press correspondent to-day
that with the murder of the
three Franciscan mission-
aries, Bishop Isai, and
Fathers Bruno and Rupertus,
the total number of Catholic
priests killed in China re-
cently was 22.—Associated
Press through Reuter.

?
Yes

4/12
MS
Foreign Section,
Please endeavour obtain any correspondence
between a list of the priests killed and
particulars of the places where they met their
deaths. The Director General of
School will probably be willing to help
W. O. S.
